name: SRCH²
tagline: In-memory instant search engine with typo tolerance, geo search and an Android SDK; abandoned since 2016.
description: SRCH2 was a commercial search engine built around the research of UC Irvine professor Chen Li on fast fuzzy and search-as-you-type queries. Written in C++ and held in memory, it served instant, typo-tolerant results through a JSON/REST API, added geo-search and record-level access control lists in 2014, and offered a thin Android SDK so search could run on the handset. The company pitched it as a faster, smaller alternative to Lucene-based engines. The source was published on GitHub under a BSD 3-clause licence in 2016, the last commit landed that May, and the company website disappeared around 2017. Typesense and Meilisearch now fill the instant-search niche.
statusNote: Company website gone since about 2017; the BSD-licensed GitHub source has had no commits since May 2016. Use Typesense or Meilisearch.

pricing.notes: Was sold as enterprise and mobile editions; only the unmaintained open-source code remains.

scale.notes: Index held in memory on one server.

strengths: Instant, typo-tolerant search-as-you-type tuned for low latency
Small enough to run inside Android apps
Built-in geo search and record-level access control
weaknesses: Abandoned: no commits since 2016 and no vendor
Index must fit in memory on one node
useCases: Historical reference for mobile on-device search
